accuracy.evidence: Lab draws displacement = A·sin(2π(x/λ − t/T)) with λ = v·T on both panels from one model, so the distance snapshot and the buoy's time record always agree; spot-checked t = 0.5 s, λ = 1.6 m, T = 2 s: crests at 0.8, 2.4, 4 m and at 0.75, 2.75 s, as the live description reports. Lesson values (amplitude = rest line to crest, wavelength = crest to crest, f = 1/T, v = λ/T, 0.25 s apart gives 4 Hz, 2 m ÷ 0.5 s = 4 m/s) checked; parameterised answers b, a, a/10, 2a, 12/a validated at range corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: crest-to-trough taken as the amplitude (p3, m6, challenge '4 cm'), crest-to-trough taken as the wavelength (p4, m3, challenge 0.6 m / 0.75 s), reading a period off a distance graph or a wavelength off a time graph (p1, m1, m9), period vs frequency swapped (m4, challenge 0.67 Hz / 0.5 s), and right number with wrong unit.

lab_distinct.evidence: Own mechanism: two linked panels (displacement–distance snapshot and displacement–time record of one buoy) with draggable measuring markers that snap to crests, troughs and zero crossings and read a gap across or up. The existing flagwave lab animates a single wave with knobs; nothing else has paired graphs or measurement markers; lab_distinct gate passed under the 30% shingle limit.

lab_teaches.evidence: Every quantity is measured by the learner, not told: they set markers to a crest and the rest line for amplitude, crest to crest on the top graph for wavelength, crest to crest on the bottom graph for period, then halve the period and watch the wavelength halve, and count waves in a 1 s marker gap for frequency. The sandbox lets them change amplitude, period and speed and check speed = wavelength ÷ period.

predictions.evidence: Seven steps with predictions before the reveal: whether amplitude is the 8 cm crest-to-trough height or 4 cm, whether a wavelength is crest-to-trough or crest-to-crest, which graph holds the period, and what happens to the wavelength when the period is halved at the same speed; each prediction is then tested by a marker task that only ticks when measured correctly.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Challenge asks for amplitude, wavelength, period or frequency of a new random wave with a number plus unit select. Tested in iPhone 13 browser: '1.2 m' for period names the wrong graph, '0.75 s' names half a wave, '0.67 Hz' names frequency vs period, '1.5 m' names a right number with wrong unit, '3 cm' names a vertical size for a horizontal quantity, '4 cm' amplitude names twice the amplitude, '0.5 s' frequency names the period; correct answers tick and offer Another.

readability.evidence: Validator Flesch–Kincaid: kid paragraphs grade 3.3, adult paragraphs grade 6.6, both under the 6.5 / 9.5 limits for a 12–14 learner. Short sentences, one idea each, units spelled out (metres, seconds, hertz), and the worked example walks one graph pair start to finish.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases; every paragraph states a reading rule, a check, or a slip. The family tip is a concrete activity (draw one wavy line, label the axis distance then time, and see crest-to-crest change from wavelength to period) rather than generic encouragement; explanation similarity to other lessons is under the 12% limit.

mobile.evidence: Pipeline walk passed at iPhone 13 (390 px) and desktop 1200×900. Screenshots show both panels readable with titles above and axis labels below, no horizontal overflow, buttons wrap into 44 px rows. A real touch drag via CDP moved marker 2 from 1 m to 2 m and marker 1 to 0.4 m, ticking the wavelength task; the Guide button only slightly covers the time axis label on phone.

accessibility.evidence: Axe clean in dark-glass and classic themes. All marker moves work from buttons (select marker, step 0.05, jump to next feature, choose graph and direction), so the amplitude task was completed with buttons only. Canvas aria-label and a live region describe crest positions, markers and gap; under reduced motion Play becomes 'Move on 0.25 s' and tweens are instant.
